comment: Provenance and reproduction recipe for the artifacts the Android station
runs. The models are NOT in this repository: each carries its own licence,
one of them is AGPL-3.0, and this repository is public and MIT — so
committing them would mean redistributing under terms it cannot offer.
This file plus scripts/fetch_edge_models.py is the substitute, and it is a
complete one: the local exports are byte-identical across runs given the
pinned versions below, which the recorded sha256s verify.
No Qualcomm AI Hub account is required. AI Hub job IDs are recorded as
provenance, but they are scoped to the account that created them, so they
are not a reproduction path for anyone else — the local export is.

yolox.note: Use the compile job's SOURCE model. Its target is an sc8380xp QNN context binary and will not load on a phone; the source is QDQ ONNX, so the QNN EP compiles it for whatever Hexagon it finds at session init.
yolox.export_command: python -m qai_hub_models.models.yolox.export --target-runtime onnx --quantize w8a8 --device 'Snapdragon 8 Elite QRD'
yolox.automation_note: Needs the `yolox` pip extra, whose build requires torch to already be installed; run it deliberately rather than from the fetch script.

pose_landmark.note: qai-hub-models has de-published mediapipe_pose as a packaged model but still ships the code and fetches the zmurez/MediaPipePyTorch weights. Float32 on purpose: pose quantization is where docs/VALIDATION.md §1's placeholder-calibration damage landed, and this HTP runs fp16 natively.

yolo26_pose.role: single-stage detector + COCO-17 pose (prototype, behind a file flag)
yolo26_pose.note: The AI Hub build is the device-optimised variant and is optional. It renames graph outputs to output_0/1/2; the fetch script restores the canonical boxes/scores/keypoints names the app's contract check expects, rather than loosening a check that exists to catch exactly this.
